newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ford Australia says report simplistic.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ford Australia says report simplistic.

text.p: Ford Motor Co of Australia Ltd said on Friday that an Industry Commission draft report on the automotive industry had failed to recognise the need to boost both investment and employment growth in Australia.
Ford Australia president David Morgan said the report had focused primarily on tariffs and described it as a "fairly simplistic treatment of a complex subject".
In its draft report on the industry, the commission said it believed tariff assistance for the domestic automotive industry should be cut to five percent by 2004 from 25 percent now.
Morgan said the draft recommendations continued the perceived association between tariff reductions and productivity and quality improvements in the industry.
"The recommendations appear to give no recognition to the value adding impact of the automotive manufacturing industry in Australia," he said in a statement.
"Where is the recognition of our unique linkages to other industries, our high tech capability and our commitment to excellence in the training and education of Australians," he asked.

Morgan noted that associate commissioner Ian Webber, former managing director of Chysler Australia Ltd and director of its successor Mitsubishi Motors Australia Ltd, preferred to maintain the tariff at 15 percent at least until 2005. Webber believed a further review was needed around 2000.
Morgan said it was telling that Webber, "the commissioner with extensive international business experience", had not supported the majority viewpoint.
He stressed that this week's report was only a preliminary draft and that the final arbiter would be the Australian government.
